categories.title: Medical & Financial Relief
categories.summary: Verified help when an illness, debt or sudden financial crisis becomes too heavy for a family to carry alone.
categories.description: When a medical emergency or sudden financial hardship pushes a family beyond what it can manage alone, Amaana Foundation steps in with carefully verified, case-specific support. Depending on the need, assistance may help with urgent treatment costs, debt relief, livelihood recovery, or other essential financial burdens. Whether support is raised publicly or arranged privately, our focus remains the same: respond with dignity, use funds responsibly, and provide clear accountability for how assistance reaches the intended family.

categories.title: Emergency & Humanitarian Relief
categories.summary: From floods to community-wide emergencies, we respond with practical support, trusted local coordination and clear accountability.
categories.description: From floods to community-wide emergencies, we respond with practical support, trusted local coordination and clear accountability.

categories.title: Ramadan & Eid Initiatives
categories.summary: Recurring programmes that turn the spirit of Ramadan, Eid and Qurbani into thoughtful support for families facing financial hardship.
categories.description: Recurring programmes that turn the spirit of Ramadan, Eid and Qurbani into thoughtful support for families facing financial hardship.

categories.title: Amaana Taleem Initiative
categories.summary: Helping learners continue with dignity through educational essentials, Qur'anic learning and verified sponsorship pathways.
categories.description: Amaana Taleem Initiative brings together practical educational assistance and faith-based learning sponsorship for children and young people whose families may struggle to meet the cost of learning. The initiative began with identifiable, verifiable needs — including stationery kits for 50 orphan children in Borabanda, Hyderabad, in 2025 — and now also facilitates continuing sponsorship for Qur'an Nazira and Hifdh day scholars. As of September 2026, 25 students across Nazira and Hifdh were being sponsored through Amaana by multiple donors. As the initiative develops, Amaana also aims to extend verified support to school and college students whose education may otherwise be disrupted by financial hardship.

categories.title: Seasonal Relief & Essentials
categories.summary: Timely, practical support for seasonal needs that can place additional pressure on already vulnerable households.
categories.description: Amaana Foundation's Seasonal Relief & Essentials programme responds to predictable hardships that become more severe at particular times of the year. The focus is simple: identify a genuine seasonal need, reach people who are least equipped to absorb the added burden, and provide useful essentials at the time they are most needed. Winter support currently forms the programme's documented starting point, with future seasonal responses able to sit within the same framework as needs are verified.

initiatives.title: A Livelihood on Wheels
initiatives.summary: Sometimes the most meaningful assistance is not temporary relief, but the means to move forward independently. Through the collective support of our donors, ₹95,000 was raised to help provide an auto-rickshaw and essential start-up support—creating an opportunity for sustained income, greater stability, and a more dignified path forward.

initiatives.title: Together for a Newborn’s Recovery
initiatives.summary: In the first days of life, one family found itself facing an unexpected medical emergency. Their eight-day-old baby boy required hospital care and C-PAP respiratory support while mounting treatment costs placed the family under severe financial strain. Amaana Foundation mobilized a medical-aid appeal, and donors responded with compassion and urgency, helping raise ₹107,520 to support the family’s medical expenses. The child later improved and was discharged from hospital—a completed appeal made possible by timely community support.

initiatives.title: Standing With Him Through Cancer Surgery
initiatives.summary: Facing stage 3 oral cancer, a patient in Hyderabad required urgent surgery at Mythri Hospital in May 2025. Amaana Foundation mobilized community support for the medical need, and donors came together to contribute ₹319,000 toward his surgery. The appeal reflects what timely collective giving can achieve when a family is confronted with a serious medical crisis.

initiatives.title: Standing With Aliza Through Critical Care
initiatives.summary: Baby Aliza Fatima Quadri developed severe pneumonia that progressed to Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) with refractory hypoxemia, leaving her in need of advanced respiratory and intensive care. After High Frequency Oscillatory Ventilation (HFOV) was unable to stabilise her condition, she required veno-venous ECMO support, mechanical ventilation, IV antibiotics, and continued treatment in the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit at KIMS Hospitals. Amaana Foundation mobilized an urgent medical-aid appeal and, through the generosity of donors, raised ₹482,700 toward her treatment. The Foundation team personally delivered the support to her family, who confirmed receipt and expressed their gratitude to everyone who stood with them during this critical period. At the time of the appeal update, Aliza remained under intensive treatment, so the fundraising appeal was completed while her medical recovery was still ongoing.

initiatives.title: Supporting a Mother Through Severe Burn Treatment
initiatives.summary: After suffering 45% severe burn injuries, a single mother of two required continued medical treatment at a time when her family had already exhausted much of its financial capacity. Around ₹4.2 lakh had already been spent on her care before the family approached Amaana Foundation for support. After reviewing the documents and verifying the case, Amaana mobilized a medical-aid appeal and raised ₹72,000. The amount was handed directly to the patient’s daughter to support the ongoing treatment need.

initiatives.title: Restoring Financial Breathing Room for an Auto Driver’s Family
initiatives.summary: An auto-rickshaw driver and father of two, was supporting his family on a modest and uncertain household income while living in rented accommodation. One son relied on irregular daily-wage work with no permanent employment, while his younger son had ongoing medical needs. Medical and household pressures had forced the family to pledge jewellery and take on debt, with interest continuing to increase the burden. After reviewing the loan paperwork and verifying the situation, Amaana Foundation chose to resolve the case privately rather than launch a public appeal. ₹138,300 was pooled by Amaana team members and friends, the outstanding loan was cleared, and the family’s pledged jewellery was released and returned.

initiatives.title: When Hyderabad Flooded, Our Community Responded
initiatives.summary: In October–November 2020, during Amaana’s early grassroots phase and before the Foundation was formally registered, the team responded to families affected by the Hyderabad floods through a three-phase relief effort. Support included ration and expanded relief kits, direct assistance to affected households, and coordinated help through trusted local organisations. Across the first two phases, 82 ration kits were distributed in Baba Nagar and Balapur and a further 60 expanded relief kits were provided for assessed flood-affected families, with Safa Baitul Maal supporting on-ground assessment and beneficiary coordination. A third phase included a designated ₹50,000 donor transfer for further relief support.

Phase 1 also supported affected households directly and through HHF, Sakina Foundation, Deccanistan and Jamaat-e-Islami Hind.
Phase 2: 60 expanded relief kits worth over ₹100,000 handed to Safa Baitul Maal for assessed families.
Phase 3: a designated ₹50,000 donor contribution transferred to Safa Baitul Maal.

initiatives.title: Responding to Families During the COVID-19 Crisis
initiatives.summary: During the COVID-19 crisis in 2020, the family-led effort that would later become Amaana Foundation responded to households facing sudden income loss, food insecurity and severe uncertainty. Alongside the first Eid Gift Kits initiative, the founding team provided ration and essential-support assistance to families in need through its local community network.
initiatives.story:
During the COVID-19 crisis in 2020, the family-led effort that would later become Amaana Foundation responded to households facing sudden income loss, food insecurity and severe uncertainty. Alongside the first Eid Gift Kits initiative, the founding team provided ration and essential-support assistance to families in need through its local community network.

These early distributions took place before Amaana had formal organizational systems and standardized annual reporting. The work forms an important part of Amaana's grassroots history, but complete beneficiary and financial totals are not available today. Rather than reconstruct figures that cannot be verified, Amaana records the initiative honestly as part of its early emergency response.

initiatives.title: Sharing the Blessing of Iftar
initiatives.summary: Dates are a simple but meaningful part of Ramadan and the breaking of the fast. Through Amaana Foundation’s Dates Distribution initiative, this small act of giving has been carried forward year after year as part of our seasonal community support. Across the four documented years from 2023 to 2026, 420 kg of dates were distributed, with the programme growing from 78 kg in 2023 to 162 kg in 2026.

initiatives.title: Eid Gift Kits — Celebrating Eid With Dignity
initiatives.summary: Amaana Foundation’s Eid Gift Kits initiative is its longest-running annual programme, beginning in Ramadan 2020 as a family-led response during the COVID period in Hyderabad. Each year, carefully assembled household packages are provided to financially vulnerable families so they can prepare for Eid with greater dignity and ease. The contents and cost of each kit are adjusted to market conditions and household needs. From 85 families in 2020 to 710 families in 2026, the initiative has recorded 2,830 family distributions across seven annual drives.

initiatives.story:
During the 2025–26 winter season, Amaana Foundation distributed 234 Winter Kits to 234 beneficiaries through a multi-phase Winter Drive. The support included sweaters, blankets and beanie caps for madrasa students, orphan children, widows, daily-wage labourers, domestic workers and other people facing seasonal hardship.

In Phase 1, support was distributed at Al Madarsatul Islamia LiTahfizil Quranil Kareem, FeelKhana, Mallepally, reaching 96 madrasa students, including boys and girls from approximately ages 2 to 18 and underprivileged orphan children. In Phase 2, Amaana worked in collaboration with Al Khair Society at Al Khair Masjid, Hyderabad, where 101 Winter Kits were distributed. These phase figures are supporting sub-measures within the overall drive and must not be added to the overall total of 234 Winter Kits distributed to 234 beneficiaries.

## Hero — Recommended Primary Copy

**Eyebrow:**  
**AMAANA FOUNDATION · HYDERABAD**

**Headline:**  
# **Trust, Turned Into Action.**

**Supporting Copy:**  
Amaana Foundation is a Hyderabad-based charitable trust helping families through verified medical and financial assistance, education support, Ramadan and Eid initiatives, seasonal relief and emergency response. We believe every contribution is an *amaana*—a trust to be handled with dignity, transparency and responsibility.

**Primary CTA:** **See Our Work**  
**Secondary CTA:** **Support a Verified Need**  
**Tertiary CTA:** **Request Assistance**

### Alternate Faith-Led Hero
**Headline:**  
**An Amaana to Serve. A Responsibility to Deliver.**

**Supporting Copy:**  
What began as a family-led Ramadan effort in 2020 has grown into a registered charitable foundation built around a simple principle: identify genuine need, respond with compassion, and remain accountable for what has been entrusted to us.

**CTAs:** **Explore Our Impact** · **Support Amaana**

### Homepage Hero Strategy Note
Lead with the meaning of *Amaana*—trust—rather than a generic charity slogan. The visitor should understand within seconds **who Amaana is, where it works, what it does and why it can be trusted**.

---

## Homepage — Trust Introduction

**Heading:**  
## **Compassion With Accountability**

**Copy:**  
Good intentions matter. So does what happens next. Amaana Foundation works close to the communities it serves, reviews needs before mobilising support, protects sensitive beneficiary information, and reports documented outcomes wherever records permit. Our responsibility is not only to collect support, but to ensure that it is directed toward the purpose for which it was entrusted.

**CTA:** **How Amaana Works**

---

## Homepage — Our Work Intro

**Eyebrow:** **OUR WORK**

**Heading:**  
## **Different Needs. One Standard of Care.**

**Copy:**  
Some needs return every year. Others arrive without warning. Amaana's work therefore combines recurring programmes with verified case-led assistance—from Eid Gift Kits and Qurbani distribution to Taleem, winter relief, emergency response and urgent medical or financial support.

**CTA:** **Explore All Initiatives**

---

## Homepage — Impact Intro

**Heading:**  
## **Impact We Can Stand Behind**

**Copy:**  
We would rather show programme-level evidence than publish one oversized number that cannot be responsibly audited. Our impact reporting focuses on documented annual reach, quantities distributed, verified cases completed and what donor support enabled.

### Recommended Homepage Impact Highlights
- **7 consecutive years** — Eid Gift Kits, 2020–2026
- **2,830 family distributions** — across seven documented Eid Gift Kit drives
- **710 families** — reached through Eid Gift Kits in 2026

14.name: About Amaana
14.source:
## Page Title
# **A Trust That Began With a Simple Decision to Help**

## Intro
Amaana Foundation is a Hyderabad-based registered charitable trust rooted in the Islamic principle of *amanah*—trust. We exist to turn compassion into practical, verified assistance while treating both donor contributions and beneficiary dignity as responsibilities entrusted to us.

---

## Our Story

**Heading:**  
## **From a Ramadan Effort to a Continuing Responsibility**

**Copy:**  
Amaana's story began in Ramadan 2020, during the uncertainty of the COVID-19 crisis. Families around us were facing lost income, rising household pressure and the prospect of Eid without the essentials many of us take for granted. What began as a family-led effort, supported by relatives and friends, helped **85 families** through the first Eid Gift Kits drive.

We could have treated that first effort as a one-time response. Instead, we returned the following year—and the year after that. The Eid programme grew from **85 families in 2020 to 710 families in 2026**, while other needs became visible through the same community networks: flood-affected households, patients facing urgent treatment costs, children needing educational support, families struggling through winter, households unable to afford Qurbani meat, and individuals needing a path back to financial stability.

As the responsibility grew, so did the need for structure. In **2023**, the family decided to formalise the work so that donations, records, governance and future programmes could be handled more consistently. Amaana Foundation was subsequently registered as a charitable trust in Hyderabad on **23 February 2024**, followed by NGO DARPAN registration in May 2024.

Today, Amaana combines the closeness of a community-rooted organisation with a growing commitment to stronger systems, transparent reporting and responsible digital infrastructure. The scale has changed. The principle has not: **what is entrusted to us must be handled with care.**

**CTA:** **See Our Journey** · **Explore Our Work**

---

## What “Amaana” Means

**Heading:**  
## **Amaana Means Trust**

**Copy:**  
Our name is more than an identity. It is a standard we try to work by. A donation is an *amaana*. A family's private documents are an *amaana*. A volunteer's time is an *amaana*. The story we tell about someone in hardship is also an *amaana*.

For us, trust means using support for its stated purpose, verifying responsibly, communicating honestly, protecting what should remain private and acknowledging clearly when a fact or figure cannot be verified.

---

15.name: Mission, Vision & Values
15.source:
## Mission
**To identify genuine need, verify it responsibly, mobilise support with integrity, deliver assistance with dignity, and account for the outcome.**

## Vision
**A community in which charitable support is trusted, dignified and capable of creating both immediate relief and meaningful opportunity.**

## Our Values

### **Amanah — Trust**
We treat donations, information and responsibilities as things entrusted to our care—not simply resources to be used.

### **Dignity**
A person should not have to surrender privacy or self-respect in order to receive help.

### **Verification**
Compassion begins the conversation; responsible review determines how we respond.

### **Transparency**
Where records permit, we report what was raised, what was delivered and what the support enabled.

### **Local Accountability**
We stay close to the communities, referrals and partners through which needs reach us.

### **Continuity**
We aim to build dependable programmes and improve them year after year rather than appearing only when a campaign is visible online.

### **Compassion With Structure**
Empathy should move us to act. Good systems help make that action responsible, fair and sustainable.

Need is assessed in context. We avoid reducing people to a category, and we do not promise assistance solely because someone fits a particular label.

17.name: How Amaana Works / How We Verify
17.source:
## Page Title
# **Verify Privately. Respond Responsibly. Report Clearly.**

## Intro
A genuine request for help often comes with deeply personal information. Amaana's process is designed to understand the need without turning private hardship into public spectacle.

## From Request to Relief

### **1. A Request or Referral Reaches Us**
Requests may come directly from a family, through trusted community contacts, masjid/community networks, social media or Amaana's assistance channel.

### **2. We Understand the Need**
The team reviews the urgency, circumstances, nature of assistance required and whether Amaana is reasonably positioned to help.

### **3. We Verify Privately**
Relevant supporting documents or corroboration may be requested. Medical records, identity documents, bank information and sensitive family details are handled as verification material—not public content.

### **4. We Decide the Appropriate Response**
Depending on the case, assistance may come through available funds, a dedicated public appeal, an in-kind programme, direct procurement or referral to another suitable organisation.

### **5. We Mobilise Support When Needed**
If a public appeal is necessary, we communicate enough information to explain the verified need while avoiding unnecessary exposure of the person or family involved.

### **6. Assistance Is Delivered**
Support may take the form of medical assistance, financial relief, food or seasonal essentials, education support, livelihood assets or other case-specific help.

### **7. We Close the Loop**
Where appropriate and documented, donors receive completion updates, distribution figures, photographs, financial summaries or confirmation of the outcome.

## Core Principle
### **Public Evidence. Private Proofs.**
We should be able to demonstrate that assistance happened and that entrusted support was used for its stated purpose without publishing documents that could compromise a beneficiary's dignity, safety or privacy.

**CTA:** **Request Assistance** · **Explore Completed Appeals**

18.name: Transparency & Accountability
18.source:
## Page Title
# **Trust Is Built in the Details**

## Intro
Transparency is not the publication of every private document. It is the discipline of being precise about what is known, what was collected, what was delivered, what remains unverified and what should remain confidential.

## How Amaana Builds Accountability
- Maintain programme and campaign records wherever available.
- Report documented quantities, beneficiary counts and campaign outcomes without inflating them.
- Preserve annual cost information for recurring initiatives such as Eid Gift Kits.
- Provide completion updates for case-led medical, financial and livelihood appeals where an outcome is documented.
- Separate operational expenses from programme donations where records make that distinction available.
- Preserve photographs and distribution evidence where publication is appropriate.
- Maintain registration and compliance information in a dedicated public area.
- Use role-based administration for the digital platform rather than relying on one shared credential.

## What We Intentionally Keep Private
- Aadhaar and other identity documents
- Medical reports, prescriptions and private clinical records
- Bank account details and sensitive transaction proofs
- Private verification conversations
- Unnecessary family details
- Children's identifying information unless publication is appropriate and approved

## Reporting Philosophy
**We prefer a smaller number we can explain over a larger number we cannot responsibly defend.**

Amaana therefore reports impact by programme and year rather than combining all activity into a single lifetime beneficiary total that could double-count the same household across different initiatives.

**CTAs:** **View Our Impact** · **See Registration & Compliance**

---

## Page Title
# **Impact, Without Inflated Numbers**

## Intro
Every number on an impact page should be able to answer a second question: **what does it represent?** Amaana therefore reports programme-level and case-level outcomes rather than collapsing unrelated activities into one marketing total.

## Recommended Impact Narrative
From **85 Eid Gift Kit families in 2020 to 710 in 2026**, Amaana's longest-running programme shows what consistent community support can build over time. Around that recurring core, other programmes have developed as verified needs emerged: Qurbani meat distribution, Ramadan dates, Taleem, winter essentials, disaster response and case-led medical, financial and livelihood assistance.

The purpose of this page is not simply to display numbers. It is to connect each figure to a documented action—a kit prepared, a family reached, a treatment need supported, a debt cleared, a student equipped or a relief response completed.

## Recommended Impact Modules
Use separate modules rather than one cumulative total:
- **Eid Gift Kits:** year-by-year 2020–2026
- **Qurbani:** 2025 and 2026 separately, plus 500+ family distributions across the two documented drives
- **Dates:** year-by-year kilograms, 420 kg across 2023–2026
- **Taleem:** 50 stationery-kit recipients in 2025; 25 Nazira/Hifdh students documented under sponsorship as of September 2026
- **Winter:** show approved drive figures and phase measures separately
- **Emergency Relief:** show Hyderabad Flood Relief phases; COVID support without invented totals
- **Case-Led Assistance:** show each completed verified case individually with amount and documented outcome

**CTA:** **Explore the Work Behind the Numbers**

23.name: Faith & Giving
23.source:
## Page Title
# **Giving as Trust, Worship and Responsibility**

## Intro
Amaana's work is inspired by Islamic teachings on charity, compassion, justice and responsibility. Faith should deepen the way we serve—not replace verification, accountability or respect for the person receiving support.

## Qur'anic Reflection
**Heading:** **Generosity That Multiplies Good**

**Copy:**  
The Qur'an describes sincere spending in the way of Allah through the image of a grain that grows into many ears, each carrying further grain (**Qur'an 2:261**). The lesson is not only about multiplication of reward; it reminds us that a sincere act of giving can continue producing benefit beyond the moment it is made.

## Hadith Reflection
**Heading:** **Charity Does Not Diminish Wealth**

**Copy:**  
The Prophet ﷺ taught that charity does not decrease wealth (**Sahih Muslim 2588**). For donors, this is an invitation to generosity with trust in Allah; for Amaana, it is also a reminder that donated wealth carries responsibility and must be handled with integrity.

## Service Reflection
**Heading:** **Helping One Another**

**Copy:**  
Prophetic teaching also connects Allah's help with a believer's willingness to help another person in need (**Sahih Muslim 2699**). Amaana seeks to translate that ethic into practical service—verify the hardship, protect dignity, and respond where we can.

### Religious Copy Implementation Note
When displaying translated Qur'an or Hadith wording verbatim, use a recognized translation/source and keep the reference visible. The summaries above are intentionally paraphrased for website use.

34.name: Frequently Asked Questions
34.source:
## How does Amaana decide whom to help?
Requests are reviewed based on the nature and urgency of the need, available verification, Amaana's charitable scope and current capacity. Submission or referral does not automatically guarantee assistance.

## Does Amaana verify medical and financial appeals?
Amaana requests relevant supporting information or corroboration before approving case-led assistance or public fundraising. Sensitive documents are kept private rather than displayed publicly.

## Why doesn't Amaana publish every proof document?
Transparency and privacy are not opposites. Amaana publishes enough information to explain the verified need and documented outcome while keeping identity documents, private medical records, bank details and sensitive family information confidential.

## Can I donate from outside India?
Amaana Foundation is not currently FCRA-registered. Its public donation flow is therefore restricted to domestic contributions unless the legal position changes.

## Does Amaana have 80G approval?
Amaana currently holds **provisional approval under Section 80G** via Form 10AC dated 26 January 2026, covering AY 2026–27 through AY 2028–29. The website should not describe this as permanent or final approval.

## Are all Amaana causes Zakat-eligible?
No. A cause should be presented as Zakat-eligible only when Amaana has specifically confirmed that status and can handle the contribution accordingly. If an appeal is not marked as Zakat-eligible, donors should not assume that it is.

## Can I request help for someone else?
Yes, referrals may be submitted, but Amaana may need to contact the affected person/family or obtain relevant information before making a decision.

## Can I volunteer?
Yes. Volunteer opportunities depend on current programmes and needs. Amaana values reliable support in logistics, documentation, education, media, technology and professional areas.

## Can an institution partner with Amaana?
Yes. Amaana is open to responsible collaborations that fit its charitable scope, compliance requirements and dignity standards.

## Why doesn't Amaana publish one total number of all people helped?
The same household may receive legitimate support through different programmes or in different years. Adding every programme count together could therefore double-count people. Amaana prefers programme-level reporting that can be explained and verified.
